signals.title: Central Bank of Ireland publishes Supplemental Guidance on Prohibition Notices under the Fitness and Probity Regime
signals.why: A guidance from Central Bank of Ireland touching boardroom-and-accountability. No explicit implementation or response deadline was extracted from the official feed.

editorial.change: Central Bank of Ireland has today published its Supplemental Guidance on Prohibition Notices under the Fitness and Probity Regime , and a related Feedback Statement on Consultation Paper 166 . The Consultation , which closed on 25 March 2026, received eight submissions from representative bodies and individuals. The Central Bank’s stakeholder webinar on the topic held during the course of the consultation was positively received by its 150 attendees. The Supplemental Guidance sets out the circumstances that a decision maker will consider when determining the nature, scope and duration of a prohibition – a measure that forbids a person from performing a controlled function in a regulated financial firm in order to protect users of financial services and the financial syste
editorial.affected: Boards, senior managers, controlled-function holders, HR, compliance, and governance committees in Ireland and the EU.
editorial.implication: The guidance clarifies how prohibition decisions are considered, making accountability, role-holder evidence, and escalation records more important.
editorial.owner: Accountable owner for boardroom accountability applicability and governance review.
editorial.action: Test current fitness-and-probity records, escalation routes, and decision evidence against the clarified expectations.
editorial.evidence: Completed control mapping, accountable owner, and evidence of supervisory-readiness review.
